# EmailCheckPro Email Deliverability Check API
> Official synchronous examples for single and batch email deliverability check by EmailCheckPro.

## Canonical resources
- [Product page](https://emailcheckpro.com/products/email): Official Email Deliverability Check product overview.
- [API documentation](https://emailcheckpro.com/api-docs): Canonical request, response, limit, and error contract.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/emailcheckpro/email-deliverability-checker-api): Official multi-language examples and OpenAPI contract.
- [Registration](https://emailcheckpro.com/register?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=emailcheckpro_email-deliverability-checker-api): Account registration and API-key access.
- [Pricing](https://emailcheckpro.com/pricing): Current product pricing.

## Product facts
- Brand: EmailCheckPro.
- Product code: `email`.
- Request `service_type`: `email`.
- API base URL: https://emailcheckpro.com.
- Authentication: X-API-Key request header.
- Input: email address.
- Processing: synchronous single or batch response.
- Examples: Python, Node.js, Go, Java, C#, PHP, Shell.

## Integration contract
- Single check: POST /api/v1/check with service_type and identifier.
- Batch check: POST /api/v1/batch-check with service_type and 1-100 identifiers, results in submission order.
- Balance: GET /api/v1/balance returns data.balance_micros.
- Envelope: code, msg, data. code=0 is a determined result.
- Undetermined: code 42200, no result data, not charged.
- Batch items carry exists; result fields appear only when exists is true.

## Current response and timeout contract

Result fields are directly in `data`: `service_type`, `identifier`, `registered`. Internal `provider`/`profile_available` are not returned. For ordered batches, `exists=false` means undetermined; never classify it as a negative. Python and Node.js select `MODE=single` (default) or `MODE=batch`; their client timeout defaults to 60 / 330 seconds and is configurable via `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. The server batch window is 300 seconds. Do not blindly repeat a potentially billed request after an uncertain timeout. The default budget is five in-flight requests and one synchronous batch.
